claim: Chronic mild unpredictable stress (CMS) is a well-established rodent model of depression.

evidence: Supported by citation to Willner, 2005

claim: Chronic social defeat stress (CSDS) is a well-established rodent model of depression.

evidence: Supported by citations to Berton et al., 2006; Golden et al., 2011; Krishnan et al., 2007; Krishnan and Nestler, 2011

claim: CMS reduced action potential (AP) firing in VTA dopamine neurons.
source: However, CMS and CSDS induce opposing changes in ventral tegmental area (VTA) dopamine neuron activity: CMS reduced action potential (AP) firing in VTA dopamine neurons (Chang and Grace, 2014; Moreines et al., 2017; Tye et al., 2013), whereas susceptibility to CSDS was accompanied by an increase in AP firing (Cao et al., 2010; Chaudhury et al., 2013; Krishnan et al., 2007; Ku and Han, 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to Chang and Grace, 2014; Moreines et al., 2017; Tye et al., 2013

claim: Susceptibility to CSDS was accompanied by an increase in AP firing in VTA dopamine neurons.
source: However, CMS and CSDS induce opposing changes in ventral tegmental area (VTA) dopamine neuron activity: CMS reduced action potential (AP) firing in VTA dopamine neurons (Chang and Grace, 2014; Moreines et al., 2017; Tye et al., 2013), whereas susceptibility to CSDS was accompanied by an increase in AP firing (Cao et al., 2010; Chaudhury et al., 2013; Krishnan et al., 2007; Ku and Han, 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to Cao et al., 2010; Chaudhury et al., 2013; Krishnan et al., 2007; Ku and Han, 2017

claim: In the CSDS model, optogenetic phasic stimulation of VTA neurons that project to the nucleus accumbens (NAc) induced susceptibility to social defeat.

evidence: Supported by citation to Chaudhury et al., 2013

claim: In the CSDS model, optogenetic inhibition of the VTA–NAc projection induced resilience.
source: In the CSDS model, optogenetic phasic stimulation of VTA neurons that project to the nucleus accumbens (NAc) induced susceptibility to social defeat, whereas optogenetic inhibition of the VTA–NAc projection induced resilience (Chaudhury et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Chaudhury et al., 2013

claim: Optogenetic phasic stimulation of VTA dopamine neurons reversed CMS-induced depressive-like behavior.

evidence: Supported by citation to Tye et al., 2013

claim: Optogenetic inhibition of VTA dopamine neurons induced behavioral despair and decreased sucrose preference in stress-naïve mice.
source: In contrast, optogenetic phasic stimulation of VTA dopamine neurons reversed CMS-induced depressive-like behavior, while optogenetic inhibition of VTA dopamine neurons induced behavioral despair and decreased sucrose preference in stress-naïve mice (Tye et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Tye et al., 2013

claim: AP firing in VTA dopamine neurons is governed by multiple voltage-dependent ionic conductances, including the hyperpolarization-activated cation current (Ih).
source: AP firing in VTA dopamine neurons is governed by multiple voltage-dependent ionic conductances, including the hyperpolarization-activated cation current (Ih), which is generated by hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated (HCN) channels (McDaid et al., 2008; Okamoto et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citations to McDaid et al., 2008; Okamoto et al., 2006

claim: The hyperpolarization-activated cation current (Ih) is generated by hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated (HCN) channels.
source: AP firing in VTA dopamine neurons is governed by multiple voltage-dependent ionic conductances, including the hyperpolarization-activated cation current (Ih), which is generated by hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated (HCN) channels (McDaid et al., 2008; Okamoto et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citations to McDaid et al., 2008; Okamoto et al., 2006

claim: There are four subtypes of HCN (HCN1-4), which mainly form homotetramers with distinct properties.
source: There are four subtypes of HCN (HCN1-4), which mainly form homotetramers with distinct properties (Wahl-Schott and Biel, 2009) and have different brain distributions (Notomi and Shigemoto, 2004).

claim: HCN subtypes have different brain distributions.
source: There are four subtypes of HCN (HCN1-4), which mainly form homotetramers with distinct properties (Wahl-Schott and Biel, 2009) and have different brain distributions (Notomi and Shigemoto, 2004).
evidence: Supported by citation to Notomi and Shigemoto, 2004

claim: Hcn1-4 mRNAs are expressed in the VTA.

evidence: Supported by citation to Monteggia et al., 2000

claim: HCN2 is the predominant HCN subunit expressed in the VTA.
source: Although Hcn1-4 mRNAs are expressed in the VTA (Monteggia et al., 2000), immunostaining for HCN protein has shown that HCN2 is the predominant HCN subunit expressed in the VTA (Notomi and Shigemoto, 2004).

claim: TRIP8b is an auxiliary subunit of HCN1-4 channels and is required for HCN trafficking and enrichment at dendrites.

evidence: Supported by citations to Han et al., 2011; Lewis et al., 2009; Lewis et al., 2011; Santoro et al., 2009

claim: Global knockout of Hcn1 or Trip8b reduced behavioral despair, but these mice did not display anxiolytic-like behaviors.

evidence: Supported by citation to Lewis et al., 2011

claim: Lentivirus-mediated shRNA knockdown of HCN1 in the dorsal hippocampus promoted both anxiolytic- and antidepressant-like effects.
source: Global knockout of Hcn1 or Trip8b reduced behavioral despair, but these mice did not display anxiolytic-like behaviors (Lewis et al., 2011), while lentivirus-mediated shRNA knockdown of HCN1 in the dorsal hippocampus promoted both anxiolytic- and antidepressant-like effects (Kim et al., 2017; Kim et al., 2012).

claim: The antidepressant-like effects of global Trip8b knockout can be reversed by reinstating TRIP8b expression in the dorsal hippocampus.

claim: Apathetic (Hcn2ap/ap) mice with a spontaneous null mutation in Hcn2 show reduced behavioral despair in the tail suspension test.
source: Apathetic (Hcn2ap/ap) mice with a spontaneous null mutation in Hcn2 show reduced behavioral despair in the tail suspension test, but these mice exhibit deficits in motor coordination and locomotion and cannot perform the forced swim test due to an inability to swim (Lewis et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citation to Lewis et al., 2011

claim: Apathetic (Hcn2ap/ap) mice exhibit deficits in motor coordination and locomotion and cannot perform the forced swim test due to an inability to swim.

evidence: Supported by citation to Lewis et al., 2011

claim: The Ih current generates pacemaker activity via permeability to cations.

claim: Enhancing Ih current increases AP firing in VTA dopamine neurons.

claim: CSDS leads to an increase in Ih current in VTA dopamine neurons in susceptible mice.

evidence: Supported by citations to Cao et al., 2010; Friedman et al., 2014

claim: CSDS leads to an even further increase in Ih current in resilient mice compared to susceptible mice.
source: CSDS leads to an increase in Ih current in VTA dopamine neurons in susceptible mice, and an even further increase in Ih current in resilient mice, but normal AP firing is achieved in resilient mice via homeostatic upregulation of voltage-gated K+ currents (Cao et al., 2010; Friedman et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to Cao et al., 2010; Friedman et al., 2014

claim: Normal AP firing is achieved in resilient mice via homeostatic upregulation of voltage-gated K+ currents.
source: CSDS leads to an increase in Ih current in VTA dopamine neurons in susceptible mice, and an even further increase in Ih current in resilient mice, but normal AP firing is achieved in resilient mice via homeostatic upregulation of voltage-gated K+ currents (Cao et al., 2010; Friedman et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to Cao et al., 2010; Friedman et al., 2014

claim: Overexpression of HCN2 in VTA dopamine neurons produced a reversal of social avoidance behavior in susceptible animals.

evidence: Supported by citation to Friedman et al., 2014

claim: Intra-VTA infusion of an Ih potentiator in susceptible animals produced a reversal of social avoidance behavior.
source: Overexpression of HCN2 in VTA dopamine neurons or intra-VTA infusion of an Ih potentiator in susceptible animals produced a reversal of social avoidance behavior, likely by a homeostatic upregulation of K+ current and the subsequent normalization of AP firing (Friedman et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Friedman et al., 2014

claim: VTA dopamine neurons are heterogeneous in their projection targets and HCN expression.

claim: In mice, neurons that project to the lateral shell of the NAc display large Ih current.

claim: Neurons that project to the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC), medial shell of the NAc, or basolateral amygdala exhibit minimal Ih current.

claim: CMS significantly decreased the time spent in the open arms in the EPM test.

claim: CMS significantly increased immobility time in the FST.

claim: The average AP firing rate in VTA dopamine neurons was significantly decreased in CMS-exposed mice.

claim: The proportion of spikes occurring within bursts was decreased in CMS-exposed mice.

claim: All neurobiotin-labeled neurons identified as dopamine neurons electrophysiologically were TH+.

claim: TdTomato and TH were completely co-localized in DAT-tdTomato mice, indicating that tdTomato expression provides faithful reporting of dopamine neurons.

claim: Retrobead-labeled neurons predominantly (95.7 ± 1.1%, n = 3 mice) were co-localized with tdTomato.

evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C

claim: The vast majority of VTA neurons projecting to the NAc lateral shell are dopamine neurons.

claim: Ih amplitude was significantly decreased in dopamine neurons from CMS-exposed mice at hyperpolarization steps to −90 mV or greater.

claim: Membrane capacitance (Cm) was not significantly different between control and CMS mice.

claim: Ih current density was significantly decreased in CMS mice compared with control mice.

claim: CMS led to a significant hyperpolarizing shift of the half-activation potential (V1/2) compared with that of control.

claim: The resting membrane conductance (Gresting) was not significantly different between control and CMS mice.

claim: Ih current was abolished by the HCN channel blocker ZD7288 (30 μM) in both the control group and the CMS group.

claim: The mean firing rate was significantly decreased in the CMS group compared with the control group in vehicle-treated slices.

claim: ZD7288 (30 μM) significantly decreased AP firing in both control and CMS-exposed groups.

claim: The mean firing rate was not significantly different between control and CMS-exposed groups in the presence of ZD7288.

claim: The firing rate (FR) suppression (%) in the control group was significantly higher than that of the CMS-exposed group.

claim: AAV2-HCN2-shRNA-eGFP was expressed in 83.9 ± 6.3% of TH+ dopamine neurons in the VTA.

claim: VTA-specific HCN2 knockdown did not significantly affect the body weight of mice.
